subject: Request: Exception for multi-year term shelter + rollback clause (AcroHealth)
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Request: Exception for multi-year term shelter + rollback clause (AcroHealth)

Hi Jordan / Vivek —

Quick escalation: AcroHealth (PROC contact below) is asking for a non-standard commercial carve that I need approval for before legal drafts the redline. High level:

- Account: AcroHealth (mid-market healthcare SaaS)
- ARR today (est): $1.1M; 3yr committed term target: $3.6M ARR-equivalent revenue over term with expected ramp in Y1
- Ask: 3-year fixed-rate commitment with the following exceptions:
  • 3-year price shelter (no unit price increases for base committed units)
  • annual uplift cap of 6% on list price for renewals/upsell pricing (they expect predictability)
  • renewal protection / "rollback" clause: if we materially underperform SLA or quality metrics in any 12-month period and they materially reduce usage, they want the ability to step down to a lower tier without paying an early termination uplift or penalty (limited to once per 12 months and capped credit at 10% of annual invoice)

Why this is time-sensitive: procurement wants commercial language in the SOW this week to align internal signoffs + their board cycle. Without an approval, legal will not accept the rollback wording or the uplift cap.

Requested approvals (explicit):
1) Exec sign-off on price shelter for 3 years (no list-rate increases on committed units)
2) Approval of uplift cap at 6% annual (we can consider 7% as counter if needed)
3) Authorization to include a conditional rollback clause limited as proposed (cap credit to 10% of annual invoice, single exercise per 12 months, requires documented SLA breach of X/metric — we will define exact metric in legal redline)

Risks / mitigations:
- Revenue dilution: small, controlled by the 10% cap and single-exercise constraint
- Abuse: require documented SLA or agreed evaluation triggers and post-event remediation plan — legal will hardcode triggers
- Precedent: likely to be referenced by other healthcare deals; recommend limited to AcroHealth and one other named account (i.e., not blanket policy)

Attachments: AcroHealth_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW with proposed language stubbed)
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ACR-2028-019

Can you advise clearance (yes/no) and any guardrails you want me to add before I send to legal/procurement? If approved, I'll patch the SOW and send to their procurement lead (Matt Green) and start DocuSign prep.

Thanks —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman | Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123
[Attachment: AcroHealth_SOW_v3.pdf]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 12:37:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: Exception for multi-year term shelter + rollback clause (AcroHealth)

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the write-up. Couple of clarifying items before I can route to Pricing/Legal properly:

1) Baseline units and seat counts: please confirm committed units by product line (embedding units, gen tokens, private model seats) that the 3-year shelter should apply to. We need precise numbers to model P&L impact.
2) SLA metric: what is the concrete trigger AcroHealth expects for the rollback? e.g., 99.5% availability monthly, or a per-month latency SLA miss threshold?
3) Credit mechanics: do they want an immediate invoice credit (our preference is credit applied to next invoice) or a future billing rate adjustment?
4) One-time exception or portfolio exception? Confirm you want this limited to AcroHealth (recommended).

Looping in Matt from their procurement on the next send.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake | Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 08:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request: Exception for multi-year term shelter + rollback clause (AcroHealth)

Naomi / Jordan —

I reviewed the ask and the proposed guardrails. Approve in principle with the following executive-level conditions:

1) Price shelter: Approved for committed baseline units only (you must enumerate baseline units per product in the SOW). No shelter on burst/overage units.
2) Uplift cap: Approve 6% annual cap on list price; however, if net usage growth across the account > 30% year-over-year, uplift cap increases to 7% for that next renewal period (protects us for outsized usage growth).
3) Rollback clause: Approve conditional rollback with strict constraints:
   • Trigger requires two consecutive months of SLA miss defined as 99.5% availability OR median p95 latency > 2s on production endpoints for 30 days (Jordan/legal to translate into exact SLO language).
   • Customer may exercise step-down once per 12-month period and only to the next available tier; exercise limited to a single tier down and capped at 10% credit of the annual invoice as requested.
   • Credits are applied as invoice credits on the following billing cycle; no retroactive rate changes to previously invoiced periods.
4) Precedent control: This approval is limited to AcroHealth only and any references to this clause in future deals require VP-level approval.
5) Credit authorization: Any credit that would exceed $50,000 requires Finance sign-off (cc: finance required on legal form).

Deliverables before we finalize:
- Jordan: enumerate baseline units and confirm shield is only for those units.
- Legal: draft redline that includes trigger language and credit mechanics.
- Naomi: confirm AcroHealth procurement (Matt) is aligned on invoice-credit flow.

I have attached a short approval memo for Deal Desk (NAF_approval_memo_20280215.pdf) that you can include in the deal folder. Once legal confirms language I'll sign the commercial addendum.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | SVP Sales, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: NAF_approval_memo_20280215.pdf]

Matt / team —

Thanks for the quick cadence. Vivek has approved the request with a few guardrails (enumerated below) — Jordan/legal will produce the redlined SOW and commercial addendum for signature. Summary of agreed principles:

- 3-year price shelter on baseline committed units only (Jordan will enumerate units in the SOW)
- Annual uplift cap: 6% (7% conditional if usage growth >30% YoY)
- Conditional rollback: one-time step-down per 12 months, must meet SLA trigger (see Vivek's note for specifics), credit applied to next invoice, capped at 10% annual invoice, credits over $50k require Finance sign-off

Next steps / timeline:
1) Jordan/legal: finalize redline by end of day Thursday, Feb 17.
2) Naomi: will send finalized SOW and DocuSign envelope to Matt on Friday, Feb 18 if redline ready.
3) AcroHealth: aim to return signed DocuSign within 5 business days to meet their board timelines.

Attachments sent with this email: DocuSign envelope prep (DocuSign_MultiYear_AcroHealth_20280215) and SOW draft (AcroHealth_SOW_v3.pdf).

Matt — please confirm acceptance of the invoice-credit flow (credit applied to next invoice) and that procurement is comfortable with the single exercise / 10% cap.

Thanks —
Naomi
